## Create denitrification equation

This script is for creating a denitrification equation from paired nitrate, soil organic carbon and denitrification data so we can predict denitrification rates using nitrate and soil organic carbon data, which are more easily measured.

## 1. Set up

Get packages.

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
```

Get data.

```{r data}
denit <- read_excel(here("Data/Denitrification_NO3_SOC.xlsx"), sheet = "for_R")
```

## 2. Run multiple regression

Visualise relationships between predictors.

```{r explore}
ggplot(denit, aes(x = NOx_mgL, y = Dw_mg_m2_hr)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

ggplot(denit, aes(x = NOx_mgL, y = Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") # Dtot looks like a better fit

ggplot(denit, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Dw_mg_m2_hr)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

ggplot(denit, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 
```

Manipulate. Make log versions of variables.

```{r manipulate}
denit <- denit %>% mutate(
  Log_Dtot = log10(Dtot),
  Log_NOx = log10(NOx_mgL),
  Log_Dw = log10(Dw_mg_m2_hr)
)

# visualise with these new variables
ggplot(denit, aes(x = Log_NOx, y = Log_Dtot, color = Site)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") # better fit

ggplot(denit, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Log_Dtot, color = Site)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 
```

Make a model with all the data. These include data from other locations in Queensland from previous studies.

```{r model}
m <- lm(Log_Dtot ~ `OC_%_` + Log_NOx, data = denit)
plot(m) # assumptions look fine

summary(m)

# equation is Log(Dtot) = 1.4360 + 0.4241 * Log(NOx) + 0.0098 * Soil_OC
# R squared adjusted = 0.58
```

Try with only Maroochy estuary data.

```{r model_maroochy_only}
denit_maroochy <- denit %>% dplyr::filter(Site %in% c("Yandina", "Blue Heart"))

# visualise
ggplot(denit_maroochy, aes(x = Log_NOx, y = Log_Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

ggplot(denit_maroochy, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Log_Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

# model
m2 <- lm(Log_Dtot ~ `OC_%_` + Log_NOx, data = denit_maroochy)
plot(m2) # assumptions look fine

summary(m2)

# equation is log(Dtot) = 1.6030 + 0.6975 * Log(NO3) + 0.0062 * Soil_OC
# R squared adjusted = 0.9117

# try with Dw
# model
m2.5 <- lm(Log_Dw ~ `OC_%_` + Log_NOx, data = denit_maroochy)
plot(m2.5) # assumptions look fine

summary(m2.5) # way worse fit - confirms that Dtot is better.
```

Why is this different to the previously calculated equation?

Try with NO3 + 3 like the original equation to see if we come up with similar results?

Also try Ln instead of Log.

```{r model_other}
denit_maroochy <- denit_maroochy %>% mutate(
  Log_NOx_plus3_ = log10(NOx_mgL + 3) 
)

# visualise
ggplot(denit_maroochy, aes(x = Log_NOx_plus3_, y = Log_Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

# model
m3 <- lm(Log_Dtot ~ `OC_%_` + Log_NOx_plus3_, data = denit_maroochy)
plot(m3) # assumptions look fine

summary(m3)

# equation is ...
# R squared adjusted = 0.84

denit_maroochy <- denit_maroochy %>% mutate(
  Ln_NOx = log(NOx_mgL),
  Ln_Dtot = log(Dtot)
)

# visualise
ggplot(denit_maroochy, aes(x = Ln_NOx, y = Log_Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

# model
m3.5 <- lm(Log_Dtot ~ `OC_%_` + Ln_NOx, data = denit_maroochy)
plot(m3.5) # assumptions look fine

summary(m3.5) # it's the same.
```

Also try with just Blue Heart data.

```{r model_blueheart}
denit_blueheart <- denit %>% dplyr::filter(Site == "Blue Heart")

# visualise
ggplot(denit_blueheart, aes(x = Log_NOx, y = Log_Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

ggplot(denit_blueheart, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Log_Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

# model
m4 <- lm(Log_Dtot ~ `OC_%_` + Log_NOx, data = denit_blueheart)
plot(m4) # assumptions look fine

summary(m4) # not enough power anymore! variables not significant

# equation is 
# R squared adjusted = 0.77
```

Therefore, use m2!
